title.narrative: ASEAN Parliamentarians for Human Rights (APHR) - Parliamentarians for Regional Actions on Democracy

description.narrative: ASEAN Parliamentarians for Human Rights (APHR) has applied to the Embassy for funding of 6,048,500 SEK to carry out the "Parliamentarians for Regional Actions on Democracy and Human Rights in ASEAN” during the period 2015-2018. The intervention aims to a) respond to human rights issues in the region, b) oversee the compliance of states’ accountability, including its human rights institutions, to their human rights obligations, c) engage key actors including civil society and victims of human rights, and relevant bodies on human rights at the national, regional, and international level by holding an effective regular dialogue, and expanding influences with other parliamentarian members in ASEAN and beyond, and d) strengthen the institutional capacity of APHR and its members.

Asean Parliamentarians for Human Rights (APHR) har ansökt om finansiering om 6.048.500 SEK för att utföra "Parlamentariker for regionala åtgärder för demokrati och mänskliga rättigheter i ASEAN" under perioden 2015-2018. Insatsen syftar till att a) svara på människorättsfrågor i regionen, b) övervaka efterlevnaden av staternas ansvar, inklusive dess institutioner för mänskliga rättigheter, till sina människorättsförpliktelser, c) engagera nyckelaktörer, däribland det civila samhället och offer för de mänskliga rättigheterna, och relevanta organ för mänskliga rättigheter på nationell, regional och internationell nivå genom att hålla en effektiv regelbunden dialog, och ökad påverkan tillsammans med andra parlamentsledamoter i ASEA och fler, och d) stärka den institutionella kapaciteten hos APHR och dess medlemmar.
Detta är ett kompletterande beslut till beslutet (nr 2015-019).
I den planerade insatsen (2015), APHR:s budgetförslag till ambassaden uppgick till 3 827 300 för perioden 2015 - 2017. Den totala budgeten var SEK 17 635 318, där ytterligare cirka SEK 12 409 032 skulle komma från Norge och till en 398 986 från Open Society Foundation (OSF). Däremot har projektet försenats på grund av det intensiva försöket till stärkt organisatorisk kapacitet 2015; några av aktiviteterna har skjutas upp. Det föreslås därför att insatsperioden förlängs med ett år, till 2018, för att ge mer tid för APHR att säkerställa långsiktig och mångsidig finansiering. Norge kommer dock inte att kunna bidra med samma andel av budgeten (68%) år 2018 och det föreslås därför att Sverige bör öka bidraget. Den totala andelen av budgeten som Sverige kan bistå med 2016 - 2018 skulle därför vara SEK 5 320 500. Totalt uppgår det svenska stödet till 6 048 500, inklusive 2015 ursprungliga bidrag. Eftersom den ursprungliga budgeten begäran kronor 3,8 miljoner var under 5 miljoner SEK gkordes bedömningen att insatsen bör ligga som ”Begränsad” insats i Trac-systement. Insatsen kommer att hållas som ”Begränsad” i Trac men det tillkommer ytterligare krav för en ”Normal bedömning, det vill säga §2.9 Översyn av Beslut om Insats och avtalsutkast, och §3.4 Kontroll av ställningstagande av revisionsberättelse. Dessa kommer att följa Sidas insatshanteringsregler.
ASEAN Parliamentarians for Human Rights (APHR) has applied to the Embassy for funding of 6,048,500 SEK to carry out the "Parliamentarians for Regional Actions on Democracy and Human Rights in ASEAN” during the period 2015-2018. The intervention aims to a) respond to human rights issues in the region, b) oversee the compliance of states’ accountability, including its human rights institutions, to their human rights obligations, c) engage key actors including civil society and victims of human rights, and relevant bodies on human rights at the national, regional, and international level by holding an effective regular dialogue, and expanding influences with other parliamentarian members in ASEAN and beyond, and d) strengthen the institutional capacity of APHR and its members.
This is a supplementary decision to the decision no.2015-019.
In the planned contribution (2015) the APHR budget of the funding proposal to Sweden was SEK 3 827 300 for the period 2015 – 2017. The total budget was SEK 17 635 318 where the additional SEK 12 409 032 would come from Norway and SEK 1 398 986 from Open Society Foundation (OSF). However, the project has been delayed due to the intensive organizational capacity strengthening in 2015; some of the activities have to be postponed. Hence it is proposed to extend the period with one year, to 2018, to allow more time for APHR to secure long-term and diverse funding. Norway will, however, not be able to contribute the same share of the budget (68%) in 2018 and it is therefore proposed that Sweden should increase the contribution. The total budget for Sweden for 2016 – 2018 would therefore be SEK 5 320 500. In total the Swedish support would add up to SEK 6 048 500, including the 2015 initial contribution. Because the initial budget request SEK 3,8 million was below SEK 5 million the assessment was done as a Limited assessment. The assessment will be kept as Limited in Trac but the additional requirements for a Normal assessment, i.e §2.9 Review of Decision on Contribution and draft Agreement and §3.4 Control of statement on audit report, will be followed in accordance with the Rule for managing contributions.

To provide core support to ASEAN Parliamentarians for Human Rights to improve human rights protection and reduce human rights violations within Southeast Asia by 2030. The overall objective of APHRs work is to contribute to the shaping of regional responses human rights and Democracy in Southeast Asia, by exercising parliamentarians' role on representation, especially for those who are vulnerable and marginalized, and providing an oversight on democracy and human rights in ASEAN and its member countries. On output level APHR aimed at achieving the following (based on logframe 2015-2017): 1) Effective monitoring and response to serious human rights issues and violations using APHR's advocacy and intervention strategies at regional and national levels. 2) Strengthened capacities and network of APHR members in adressing human rights issues at regional and national levels. 3) Improved colloboration and partnerships with key human rights actors, mechanisms and policymakers at global, reginal and national levels. 4)Effective APHR Board and Secretariat staff capable of managing and coordinating APHR's priorities and programs based on established guidelines and systems.
